hair-follicle.def: A hair is a strand of dead cells filled with hard keratin; it grows from a hair follicle, a tube of epidermis that dips into the dermis. The shaft projects above the skin and the root lies in the follicle; the matrix in the bulb, over the hair papilla, divides to make the hair, whose layers are the medulla, cortex and cuticle.

arrector-pili.def: A small bundle of smooth muscle running from a hair follicle to the papillary dermis. Cold or fear makes it contract involuntarily, pulling the slanted hair upright and raising a goose bump.

sebaceous-gland.def: An oil gland in the dermis, usually emptying into a hair follicle, that secretes by the holocrine mode. Its product, sebum, is a mix of lipids and cell debris that keeps hair supple, slows water loss and slows some bacteria and fungi.

sweat-glands.def: Coiled tubular glands, also called sudoriferous glands. Eccrine glands, over almost all skin, open at surface pores and make watery sweat; apocrine glands, in the armpits and groin, open into hair follicles from puberty and make a thicker secretion that bacteria turn into body odor.

nail.def: A plate of hard keratin made by the nail matrix under the nail root. The visible nail body slides over the nail bed; the lunula is the visible white edge of the matrix, the eponychium (cuticle) seals its base, and the hyponychium seals under its free edge.

hair-growth-cycle.def: The repeating cycle of a hair follicle: anagen (growth, years on the scalp), catagen (a few weeks in which the follicle shrinks and a club hair forms) and telogen (about 3 months of rest before the old hair is pushed out by a new one).
